responseMessage:
Alright, chef. What do you have on hand? If you’re low-key stocked, I’d do something easy but cozy so you don’t blow up your routine.

If you’ve got chicken: do a quick honey soy garlic chicken. Slice it thin, pan sear, splash of soy, honey, a little vinegar, garlic. Let it get sticky. Throw it over rice with some frozen broccoli. Twenty minutes, tastes like you tried.

If you’ve got eggs: breakfast-for-dinner. Fried egg on crispy tortillas with black beans, salsa, avocado if you have it. Or just a loaded scramble with whatever veggies are dying in the drawer and cheese. Hot sauce makes it feel intentional.

If you’ve got pasta: lemon butter pasta with peas. Boil pasta, save a mug of pasta water, melt butter, garlic, lemon zest, pepper flakes. Toss it all with peas and parm. It’s bright and stupid easy.

If you’ve got nothing: tuna melt. Mix canned tuna with a little mayo, mustard, pickles or relish if you’ve got it. Pile on bread with cheese, press it in a pan till it’s melty. Tomato soup on the side if there’s a can lurking.

I’m over here roasting sweet potatoes and it smells so good I keep opening the oven like that does anything. I’m gonna throw them with chickpeas, spinach, and a garlicky yogurt sauce. Low effort, high payoff. This is a keep-it-steady kind of dinner night. Keep it simple and satisfying so you don’t spiral into delivery hell.
